h3_prompt:
Subject: Landscape 16:9, one continuous 11-second single-character narrative. Show exactly one physical instance of MOUSE-EAR-MUTANT-001 from Picture 1. Preserve her short white hair with eye-covering fringe and small top curl, exactly two short translucent pale-purple mouse ears attached directly to the sides of the skull, small slender body, pale oversized tunic with dark trim, cross-body strap, existing side bag and oversized dark shoes. Every reference view represents the same single character. Keep her identity, proportions, ear topology, clothing, carried items, materials and reference colors unchanged.

Movement: From 0 to 2 seconds she stands in a stable forward-facing route posture with both feet planted; an earlier harmless cue has already ended before this clip and her attention is forward. From 2 to 4 seconds one soft off-screen sound repeats once from the same side and at the same mild intensity, with no visible source and no new information. From 4 to 6 seconds only the nearer mouse ear pivots toward the sound while her torso, shoulders, pelvis, hands and feet remain still. From 6 to 8 seconds her eyes make one brief sideways check and her head begins only a tiny turn, then stops before completing a second full response. From 8 to 10 seconds her shoulders make one small settling movement back into the original forward alignment; her hands remain quiet and she does not step toward the sound. From 10 to 11 seconds the ear, eyes, head and shoulders stop moving, both feet remain planted, and the result is a clear forward-oriented refusal to reopen the completed response.

Scene: Picture 2 defines SCENE-08, the established heterogeneous-village environment, its existing elements, usable space, spatial continuity and original two-color dominant relationship. The sound source remains outside the frame. Do not invent a person, creature, building, door, machine, prop, route, reflection figure or unseen reverse view.

Camera: One locked eye-level full-body medium-wide three-quarter view in a 16:9 landscape frame. Keep both mouse ears, eyes, head, shoulders, pelvis, both feet, existing side bag and supported scene layers readable together. Fixed framing, focal length, axis and horizon; no push, pull, pan, tilt, tracking, reframing, close-up, cut, transition or split screen.

Lighting: Preserve Picture 1 materials and Picture 2 palette logic under one fixed soft diffuse light. Maintain clear two-dimensional shapes and readable separation without imposing a new palette. No new glow, flashing, relighting, weather change, sudden saturation shift or color redesign.

Atmosphere: She clearly hears the repeated request for attention but does not let unchanged information take control of her whole body again. The intended impression is selective attention rather than fear, numbness or failure to hear. Use restrained hand-drawn motion, clean line-and-shape separation, quiet pacing and a clear ear-to-eye-to-head sequence.

Audio: Ambient soundscape: low village room tone, faint air and subtle cloth presence, with exactly one mild off-screen sound during 2 to 4 seconds; no visible source. Emotional sound cue: one very sparse non-melodic tonal lift during the ear-and-eye confirmation, returning immediately as her shoulders settle; no lyrics and no strong beat. Audio supports spatial direction, action readability and restrained emotion only; it does not drive cuts and is not music-video editing.

Negative: exactly one character and one physical body, no duplicate character, no second human figure, no split screen, no clone or mirror-double, no reflection person, no crowd, no NPC, no visible sound source, no invented creature, no extra limbs, no extra ears, no wings or back-mounted appendages, no text overlay, no watermark, no abrupt redesign, no route change, no approach toward the sound, no full body turn, no full second head turn, no fear recoil, no repeated adjustment, no camera movement, no cut, no transition, no weather change, no abrupt color shift, no lyrics, no strong beat, no MV editing, no glossy 3D rendering.
